questions.question: Who among the following was the President of India when the National Emergency was declared in 1975?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed** the President of India when the National Emergency was declared in 1975.
 
• The Indian Emergency was a 21 month period beginning from 25th June 1975 to 21st March 1977.
 
• On the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed declared a state of emergency under Article 352 of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution stipulates three types of emergencies-
 
 
• National Emergency- Under Article 352, the president can declare a national emergency when the security of India or a part of it is threatened by war or external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• Constitutional Emergency- Under Article 356, empowers the President to issue a proclamation if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution.
 
• Financial Emergency- Article 360 empowers the president to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of silicon dioxide?

options.text: It is a good conductor of electricity.
It has a high melting point.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has a high melting point.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

Important Points__**

 
• SiO2 is an oxide of silicon.
 
• The chemical name is Silicon Dioxide.
 
• It is also called **Silica, Silicic oxide or silicic acid.**
 
• **Properties of silicon dioxide:**
 
 
• It is not soluble in water.
 
• It is a bad conductor of electricity.
 
• It is hard in nature.
 
• It has a high melting point.
 
• The molecular weight of SiO2 is 60.08 g/mol.
 
• The density of Silicon Dioxide is 2.648 g/cm³.
 
• The melting point of Silicon Dioxide is 1,713 °C.
 
• The boiling point of Silicon Dioxide is 2,950 °C.
 
 
 
• **Hence option 4 is the correct answer. **

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: How many natural isotopes of carbon are there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Isotopes are species of a chemical element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
 
• **C-12, C-13 and C-14** are the isotopes of carbon.
 
• **Hence there are three isotopes of carbon.**
 
• Among them, C-12 and C-14 are used in carbon dating techniques.
 
• C-13 is a stable isotope of carbon.
 
• It is used in **NMR spectroscopy.**

questions.question: Vikramaditya VI, whose court poet Bilhan wrote his biography, was the ruler of the ________ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramaditya VI**, whose court poet Bilhan wrote his biography, was the ruler of the Chalukya dynasty.

 
• The Chalukya dynasty was established by Pulakeshin I in 543.
 
• Pulakeshin I took Vatapi (modern Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka) under his control and made it his capital.
 
• Pulakeshin I and his descendants are referred to as "Chalukyas of Badami".
 
• The earliest dynasty, known as the "Badami Chalukyas", ruled from Vatapi (modern Badami) from the middle of the 6th century. 
 
• **Bilhana **was a Sanskrit writer and a well-known Kashmiri poet.
 
 
• He was born in Kavi Bilhana in the middle of the 11th century.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pallava Dynasty **existed from 275 CE to 897 CE.
 
• The Pallava Dynasty was a ruling portion of southern India.
 
 
• The capital of the Pallava Dynasty was Kanchipuram.
 
• Pallavas are most noted for their patronage of architecture and they have established the foundations of medieval South Indian architecture. 
 
 
 
• Dantidurga was the founder of the Rashtrakutas dynasty.
 
 
• He is said to have conquered Kalinga, Kosala, Kanchi, Srisril, Malava, Lata, etc., and occupied Maharashtra by defeating Chalukya King Kirtivarma.
 
• Krishna I was the son and successor of Dantidurga.
 
• He conquered the territories that were still under the Chalukyas.

questions.question: In August 2020, who among the following was the chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Om Birla.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio President of the Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG).
 
• And Shri Om Birla is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 
 
• **So, Om Birla was the chairman of the Indian Parliamentary Group.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Indian Parliamentary Group

 
 
• It is an autonomous body whose membership is open to all current or former members of the Indian Parliament.
 
• It was established in 1949 after a resolution adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 16 August 1948.
 
• The objective of the group is to promote personal contacts between Members of Parliament and to disseminate information to Members of Parliament by organizing seminars etc. on possible issues before the Parliament.
 
• It arranges lectures on political, defence, economic, social and educational problems and also arranges foreign visits with a view to develop contacts with the members of other parliaments.
 
• The group acts as a link between the Parliament of India and the various Parliaments of the world by exchange of delegations, goodwill missions, correspondence, documents etc. with foreign parliaments.

questions.question: Which of the following items does not directly affect the current account balance of India?
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is __**Revenue Income**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **current account balance** of payments is a record of a **country's international transactions with the rest of the world.**
 
• The current account includes all the transactions (other than those in financial items) that involve economic values and occur between resident and non-resident entities.
 
• **Revenue Income** - Government revenue or national revenue is money received by a government from taxes and non-tax sources to enable it to undertake government expenditures.
 
• **Net foreign income, foreign aid,** and** trade gap** are all concerned with a country's international transactions with the rest of the world.
 
• **Since the revenue income is not a country's international transaction, therefore, it does not directly affect the current account balance of India.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade gap **is a situation in which a country buys more from other countries than it sells to other countries. It is the amount of money by which a country's imports are greater than its exports.
 
• **Foreign aid** is the international transfer of capital, goods, or services from a country or international organization for the benefit of the recipient country or its population.

questions.question: Which of the following state of matter is also known as Bose-Einstein condensate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Bose-Einstein Condensate is called the Fifth state of matter.
 
• It is formed when a gas of bosons having low densities is cooled to absolute zero temperature.
 
• At this temperature, the atoms stop moving.
 
• They thus clump to each other acting like a single atom with the whole group having identical physical properties.
 
• Plasma is a subset of gas which unlike the ordinary gases, is made up of atoms where some or all the electrons are stripped and positively charged protons roam freely.

• Gas

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wimbledon.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Wimbledon__, is the oldest Grand Slam tennis tournament.
 
• It was started in 1877.
 
• This grass court tennis grand slam is the oldest of all four of these tennis events.
 
• The oldest, still-active tennis tournament in the entire world, it is looked at by many in the tennis world as the most prestigious, and it is usually held from late June to early July.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• There are four Grand Slam tournaments in Tennis viz. Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open. 
 
• These are the biggest tennis events of the year.
 
• US open
 
 
• It was started in 1881.
 
• It is held annually, starting on the last Monday in August, and lasting for two weeks into September, with the middle weekend coinciding with the Labor Day holiday.
 
• This tournament is played on a hard court.
 
 
 
• French Open
 
 
• It was started in 1891. 
 
• It is also known as the Roland Garros tournament.
 
• It was held over two weeks between late May and early June in Paris.
 
• This tournament is played on clay courts.
 
 
 
• Australian Open
 
 
• It was started in 1905. 
 
• This tournament is held annually in Melbourne over the fortnight of January.
 
• It is played on hard courts. 
 
• The tournament holds the record for the highest attendance at a Grand Slam event.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations was established earlier than the other three organizations during the British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **The Brahmo Samaj** was formed in **1828.**

 
 
• It prohibited all forms of idolatry and sacrifice, believed in the Upanishads and forbade its members from criticising other religious practices.
 
 
 
• **The Prarthana Samaj **was founded in **1867 in Bombay by Dr Atmaram Pandurang.**
 
 
• It was an off-shoot of Brahmo Samaj.
 
• It was a reform movement within Hinduism and Justice M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined it in **1870 **and infused new strength to it.
 
 
 
• **Paramahansa Mandali **was a secret socio-religious group,** established in 1849,** in Bombay and is closely related to Manav Dharma Sabha.
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj **(Truth-seekers' Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on** 24 September 1873.**
 
• **Hence Brahmo Samaj was established earlier than the other three organizations.**
